[[File:Sakurai-jinja (Sakai, Osaka), shinmon.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shinmon}}]]
{{nihongo|'''Sakurai Shrine'''|桜井神社}} is a Shinto shrine in Katakura, Minami Ward, {{ill|Sakai|Q193428|qid=Q193428}}, Osaka. It is a shikinaisha and formerly ranked as a fusha. Also known as "Niwadani Hachimangu," it is notable because its haiden is the only {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795}} building in Sakai City. {{nihongo|'''Sakurai Shrine'''|桜井神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* Central hall: {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}
* East hall: {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}
* West hall: {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}

== History ==
Tradition says the Sakurai-no-Ason clan of this area began the shrine by worshiping their ancestor {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}, and that a Hachiman deity was merged in 597.

In the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' (927), "Sakurai Shrine" is listed in Otori District, Izumi Province. Yamai Shrine and Kuni Shrine, later merged into this shrine, were also listed as shikinaisha.

In 1337, local lord Ueno Tsuneyoshi rebuilt shrine buildings. In 1577, war damage during Oda Nobunaga's Kishu campaign destroyed most buildings except the haiden, and shrine lands were confiscated. Reconstruction progressed from 1588 through the Genroku era.

During shinbutsu bunri in 1868, Buddhist images and sutras were moved out; the Amida hall was relocated, and the bell tower was later converted into a mikoshi storehouse. The shrine became gosha in 1872 and was promoted to fusha in 1942.

== Precinct ==
[[File:Sakurai-jinja (Sakai, Osaka), haiden-2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Rear view of haiden}}]]
* Honden - rebuilt 1881
* Heiden
* Chumon - built 1931
* Haiden (wari-haiden, National Treasure) - early Kamakura period; kirizuma style with tiled roof
* Emaden
* Mikoshi storehouse (former bell tower built in 1731)
* Shrine office
* Shinmon - rebuilt 1702

== Festivals ==
"Kami-Niwadani Koodori" is dedicated during the autumn festival (first Sunday of October).

== Cultural properties ==
== National Treasure ==
* Haiden (building): designated as specially protected building in 1917; designated National Treasure under the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties in 1953.

== Nationally selected intangible folk cultural property ==
* Kami-Niwadani no Koodori (selected 1972)

== Osaka Prefecture designated cultural properties ==
* Wooden deity statues (sculpture group)
* Stone lantern (made 1412)
* Kami-Niwadani no Koodori (intangible)

== Access ==
From Nankai Semboku Line Izumigaoka Station, Nankai Bus:
* Route 23 (toward Hata): get off at "Sakurai Jinja-mae" (immediate)
* Route 24 (toward Hachigamine): get off at "Katakura" (about 5 minutes on foot)
